reconcile.connective: Commentators read Luke's "all" as summarizing the main substance of Jesus's ministry, not an exhaustive inventory — the same limitation John himself concedes.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible lists these as a flat Yes/No contradiction, reading Luke's "all" against John's own admission that much went unrecorded.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999), contra/everything.html

excerpts.excerpt_text: The four evangelists, and Luke particularly, have handed down to us all that Jesus began both to do and to teach; not all the particulars - the world could not have contained them; but all the heads, samples of all, so many, and in such variety, that by them we may judge of the rest.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly bridges both verses: explains Acts 1:1's 'all' as covering only 'the heads, samples of all' rather than every particular, explicitly invoking that 'the world could not have contained' a literal full record — echoing John 21:25's own wording.

excerpts.excerpt_text: The historian suggests, that his former treatise took in the main and principal things Jesus did and taught, until such time that he ascended to heaven:
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Independently glosses Luke's opening 'all' as only 'the main and principal things' Jesus did and taught, not an exhaustive record — same harmonizing move as MHC, distinct voice and verse.

pd_work.resource: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-1714), on Acts 1:1
pd_work.author: Matthew Henry
pd_work.note: Henry's own note on Acts 1:1 (already the reconcile pole's primary excerpt) reconciles Luke's 'all' with John 21:25's admission that the world could not contain a full record. Haley's An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874) does not treat this passage — confirmed by a full-text search of the archive.org OCR text for 'former treatise,' 'Theophilus,' 'world itself,' 'could not contain,' and 'many other things,' all zero hits.
